gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Every stroke in Vast Shadow is cut to one width, diagonals included. Noto Sans Arabic is the quiet one, with a pronounced x-height and wide openings; the heading grabs attention, the body keeps things moving.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Vast Shadow keeps a constant stroke weight with no sparkle at all, just a tall mean line and generous side space. Noto Sans Armenian follows in a plain sans, its round letters wide and inviting.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Noto Sans Avestan has a pronounced x-height and curves whose tips never touch, so it feels modern and clean. Vast Shadow, meanwhile, draws diagonals just as thick as its upright strokes, which gives its headings a vintage punch.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Vast Shadow gives every stroke a pipe-like body, with a tall mean line and plenty of space around each letter. Make it small and that vintage presence fades, while Noto Sans Balinese stays short-ascendered.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Vast Shadow presses its strokes like twine into a flat surface, vintage and eye-catching with a tall mean line. Noto Sans Bamum is its opposite: open and modern.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Monoline from stem to serif, Vast Shadow looks vintage and sits tall on its mean line. Noto Sans Bassa Vah brings the opposite strength: a dominant midsection and an open-jawed c, so the pairing is a loud, showy heading beside a contemporary sans-serif.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-batak: Noto Sans Batak reads big and friendly, its x-height towering like a stubby carpenter's pencil stroke. And Vast Shadow lays down a ruler-drawn, constant-width line above it, vintage and loud while the sans keeps a wide-open e.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Noto Sans Bengali keeps capitals barely taller than lowercase, with distinctly open letter mouths. And Vast Shadow, with no hairline-to-stem shift, sits above it like a vintage sign over a quiet shopfront.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksuki: Noto Sans Bhaiksuki reads approachable, its lowercase swollen like rope coiled tight, with open apertures that are easy to follow. Vast Shadow bends its lines like tubing for a vintage shout, while the plain sans simply carries the text.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Eye-catching and vintage, Vast Shadow has a blunt round-tip marker feel from end to end. Noto Sans Brahmi sits beside it quietly, mean line set high and every curve open-ended, so one shouts and the other murmurs.
